clue.text: Revenue including award close to unbelievable

parts.note: INC is the standard abbreviation for including
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

indicators.note: close to means only the final letter of the following word is used

explanation.surface: Someone's earnings are boosted by a prize that seems scarcely credible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' looks like a containment signal, but it is simply abbreviated to INC.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue and earnings are synonyms: money coming in to a person or business.

clue.text: At home, tight-knit group pens note privately?

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: pens means encloses, as a pen holds animals, so the group goes round the note

parts.note: a sect is a close-knit faction
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A close group at home writes a message out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writes, but it means encloses.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means confidentially, out of public view, which privately also conveys.

clue.text: Tribal lot round port producing kind of trumpet

indicators.note: round means the tribal group surrounds the port

parts.note: a clan is a tribal family group
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: A tribe encircling a harbour plays a brass instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a medieval trumpet with a shrill, clear tone.

clue.text: Drink and spoil a ceremonial event almost in Georgia

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

indicators.note: in means the preceding pieces go inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Having a drink ruins a ceremony in Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final letter of the ceremony word; GA is the US postal code for Georgia, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of tequila and lime, so an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Means of communication developed in chalet

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters have been worked up into a new form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A way of keeping in touch has been set up in a holiday chalet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges IN and CHALET together.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone service where callers talk to one another is a way of communicating.

clue.text: Hot and bothered author in hotel, irritatingly sanctimonious

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

indicators.note: bothered means disturbed or flustered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A writer gets flustered in a hotel, smugly superior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' gives H; 'bothered' rearranges AUTHOR, IN and HOTEL together.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone smugly convinced of their own superior virtue.

clue.text: Section of libretto's captivating in opera

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of the words of a work is enthralling in the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition 'in opera' cannot stand for the answer; 'in' is a link word and 'opera' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Puccini's opera about a singer in Rome.

clue.text: Fashionable to conceal trouble at rising type of restaurant

indicators.note: to conceal means the fashionable word holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: in means fashionable

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A trendy place hides problems as things improve.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' reads the trouble-plus-at letters from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant serving pasta and pizza is one kind classed by cuisine.

clue.text: Admission in course of dinner?

definitions.meaning: the right of entry to a place or group
a dish served at a meal, the main one in the US

explanation.surface: Getting into a dinner during one of its stages.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the privilege of entry; the other is a dish in a meal.

clue.text: A sincere canon's arranged initial survey

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: An honest clergyman has organised a preliminary inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges ASINCERECANONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Military scouting or exploration done before action is a preliminary survey.

clue.text: Flight case?

parts.note: a flight of stairs is housed in its case, the shaft around it, not luggage for an air journey

explanation.surface: Reads like a sturdy box for carrying gear on an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' is stairs, not air travel; 'case' is the enclosing shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical shaft enclosing a staircase in a building is literally what contains a flight of steps.

clue.text: Stylish seconds displayed by marketplace

parts.note: a mart is a market or trading place

explanation.surface: Fashionable reject goods are on show at the market.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylish and the answer both mean neatly fashionable in dress or appearance.

clue.text: US city showing elegance in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish elegance
ago means at a time before now

explanation.surface: An American city that used to display refinement.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the large city in Illinois on Lake Michigan.

clue.text: First woman carrying official document recalled as devious

indicators.note: carrying means the first word holds the next piece within it

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible

indicators.note: recalled is taken as called back, so the document's letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: a visa is an official travel document

explanation.surface: Eve, holding her papers, is remembered as a sly character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' looks like remembered, but it means called back, so the document is read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Devious and the answer both describe someone avoiding directness or honesty.

clue.text: Tedium of bridge opponents facing night in Calais without end

parts.note: East and North are partnerships' seats at bridge, opponents of one another

indicators.note: without end means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: nuit is French for night, Calais being a French port

explanation.surface: Boredom of card players sitting through a long French evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without end' removes the T of NUIT, leaving NUI.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedium and the borrowed French word both mean listless boredom.

clue.text: Perhaps fat Greek character will accompany one in river

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: in means the numeral goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in England
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A plump Greek joins someone in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' signals that fat is one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fat is one example of a substance the body takes in for nourishment.

clue.text: Mutual action in The Caretaker, for instance? Not initially

indicators.note: Not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: The Caretaker is a play by Harold Pinter

explanation.surface: Characters reacting to each other in a famous stage drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not initially' removes the P of PINTER PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means reciprocal action and influence between things.

clue.text: Loathsome act surrounding trial

indicators.note: surrounding means the act's word goes around the trial's word

parts.note: a deed is an act
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A repulsive deed is wrapped around a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hated intensely is regarded as loathsome.

clue.text: Noted painting represented animals round circle

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
represented is read as re-presented, so the letters are set out anew

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A famous canvas depicting creatures around a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' rearranges ANIMALS, and 'round' puts those letters about O.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Leonardo da Vinci's portrait in the Louvre, the world's most famous painting.

clue.text: Cockney has to enter old stronghold that's rather inferior

indicators.note: to enter means the dropped-H word goes inside the stronghold

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold
a Cockney drops the H, so has becomes 'as

explanation.surface: A Londoner gets into an ancient castle that is second-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop initial H, so 'has' becomes AS.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something only loosely deserving its name, so mediocre or inferior.

clue.text: Crucial factor for a chef in style

definitions.meaning: a cook must judge flavour, so the sense of the palate is essential
refined judgement in matters of beauty or fashion

explanation.surface: What matters most to a cook is flair.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the flavour sense on the tongue; the other is aesthetic discernment, as in good dress sense.

clue.text: 'Small' bet with grand in boastful style

indicators.note: in means the grand letter goes inside the bet

parts.note: a wager is a bet
G stands for grand, slang for a thousand

explanation.surface: A modest wager placed with a thousand, made with a strut.
explanation.definitionFit: A confident, arrogant manner of walking or behaving is a boastful style.

clue.text: Managed to get on top of St Paul's, say, briefly — that's irregular

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting on top of means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

indicators.note: briefly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: St Paul's Cathedral in London is famous for its dome

explanation.surface: Someone contrives to climb to the summit of the cathedral, oddly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts DOME to DOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Something haphazard, lacking pattern or order, is irregular.

clue.text: A voluntary group see ship in confusion

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
lo is an old word meaning look or see
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A band of volunteers watches a vessel amid chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means bewildered, unsure what to do, so in confusion.

clue.text: Maybe Indian company brought up English article

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An Indian firm raises an English object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like a person, but it is the Indian Ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indian is one example of the great bodies of sea water.

clue.text: Car and tree obscured row of houses

indicators.note: obscured suggests the original words are disguised, so their letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A parked vehicle and a tree hide a street from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obscured' rearranges CAR and TREE together.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain the word names a line of houses joined side by side.

clue.text: Motivated swarm of people

definitions.meaning: past tense of a verb meaning pushed or impelled
a crowd moving together in a mass

explanation.surface: A crowd spurred into action.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the past tense of a verb for impelling; the other a noun for a large moving crowd.

clue.text: 'Knight time' — humorous feature in advertising?

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight
an eon is a vast stretch of time
light entertainment is amusing rather than serious

explanation.surface: A jokey slogan about evening hours appearing in an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight time' teases night-time, but the knight is just N.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing gas-filled tubes are a classic part of shop signs and illuminated adverts.

clue.text: Term in EU devised for one defying authority

indicators.note: devised suggests the letters are worked out into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A word coined in Brussels for a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devised' rearranges TERMINEU.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor or soldier who rebels against officers openly defies authority.

clue.text: Cross mongrel

definitions.meaning: a cross is offspring bred from two different varieties
a mongrel is an animal of mixed breed

explanation.surface: An angry dog of mixed breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, but it is the noun for a crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name the offspring of mixed parentage, plant or animal.
